newsitem.title: UK: CU nine month profit hit by weather losses.
newsitem.headline: CU nine month profit hit by weather losses.

text.p: British general and life insurer Commercial Union on Wednesday reported a slide in operating profits for the first nine months of this year and blamed increased weather losses in the United States and Britain.

Nine month operating pre-tax profits fell to 348 million pounds ($575 million) from 384 million. But CU noted that a strong performance from its European businesses helped offset the 62 million pounds increase in the weather claims.

"A strong third quarter result, with pre-tax operating profits broadly similar to last year, led to a good underlying performance at the nine months stage, in spite of the substantial increase in weather claims earlier in the year," said chief executive John Carter in a statement.
"Increased profits were achieved in France and the Netherlands and our life operations continued to make good progress with strong growth in new business," he said.

In Britain, where oversupply and the advent of direct selling techniques has intensified competition and dragged rates lower over the last two to three years, CU's general insurance premium income fell by 12 percent.
"The rating environment remains competitive, although there are signs of competition reducing in the motor classes," the company said of the British market. ($1=.6050 Pound)
